senses.sense_definition: Something attractive, tempting, or seductive that entices or induces someone to do something, especially something wrong or unwise.

examples.text: The chocolate cake on the kitchen counter was a constant <w>temptation</w> for him while he was on a diet.
She managed to resist the <w>temptation</w> to buy the expensive shoes she saw in the window.

senses.sense_definition: The state or condition of being tempted, or the desire to do something wrong or unwise.

examples.text: He felt a strong <w>temptation</w> to look at his phone during the important exam.
When faced with <w>temptation</w>, it is important to remember your long-term goals.

senses.sense_definition: The act of tempting or enticing someone to do something.

examples.text: The deliberate <w>temptation</w> of the consumers through clever advertising is a common marketing strategy.
She believed that the active <w>temptation</w> of others was a moral failing.

senses.sense_definition: Pressure applied to one's thinking designed to create wrong emotions which will eventually lead to wrong actions.

examples.text: In theological discussions, <w>temptation</w> is often described as an internal battle against negative thoughts.
The sermon focused on how to recognize the subtle <w>temptation</w> that leads to unethical behavior.
